chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while I was in Medina after returning from Mecca, 'I intend to perform Hajj on behalf of my daughter.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So make that for her, now.'
ai.seo_question: Can one perform Hajj on behalf of a living relative, such as a daughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of performing Hajj on behalf of female relatives, specifically highlighting the Imam’s instruction to designate the current pilgrimage for the daughter’s benefit. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that Hajj can be performed by proxy for those who are unable to go themselves, reflecting the broader principle of substituting religious duties for the incapacitated or deceased.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I was in Al-Medina after having had returned from Makkah, ‘I intend to perform Hajj on behalf of my daughter’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So make that to be for her, now’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al- Harith ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following:
“I once said to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in al-Madinah after my return from Makkah that I wanted to assign my al-Hajj for my daughter. He (the Imam) said, ‘Assign it for her now.’”
